bio.en: Emily Kramer is a B2B marketing leader who built and led the early marketing teams at Asana, Carta, Ticketfly, and Astro (acquired by Slack), writes the popular MKT1 newsletter, and now advises, invests in, and runs a fund for early-stage B2B startups.
bio.zh: Emily Kramer 是一位 B2B 营销负责人，曾在 Asana、Carta、Ticketfly 和 Astro（被 Slack 收购）从零搭建并带领早期营销团队，运营广受欢迎的 MKT1 通讯，现在为早期 B2B 初创提供顾问、投资，并管理一支相关基金。

summary.en: Emily introduces a "fuel vs. engine" framework for marketing: fuel is the content and value you create, while the engine is how you distribute it to the right people, and the first step before hiring is diagnosing which side is your biggest constraint. For your first marketing hire she recommends a "pie-shaped" (π) generalist who is an expert in one of product, content, or growth marketing, proficient in a second, and able to set strategy across all three. In product-led growth, marketing—not just product—should own top-of-funnel and web conversion, with clear DRIs and a smooth marketing-to-product handoff so the user experience stays consistent. She stresses judging a marketing team by impact goals and full-funnel conversion rates rather than activity metrics, and using lightweight frameworks like AOR (areas of responsibility) lists and GACCS briefs to align marketing and product. Finally, she shares how functional experts can become sought-after angel investors by articulating one clear, specific value-add—such as helping founders build their marketing function.
summary.zh: Emily 提出了一个营销的"燃料 vs 引擎"框架：燃料是你创造的内容和价­值，引擎是你如何把这些送到对的人手里，而在招人之前的第一步，是诊断哪一侧是你最大的瓶颈。关于第一个营销招聘，她推荐招一个"π 型"通才——在产品、内容、增长三类营销中有一项是专家、第二项是熟手，并且能在三者之上定战略。在产品驱动增长（PLG）里，拥有漏斗顶部和网页转化的应该是营销、而不只是产品，并且要有清晰的 DRI 和顺畅的"营销到产品"衔接，让用户体­验保持一致。她强调要用"影响目标"和全漏斗的转化率、而不是"活动指标"来衡量一个营销团队，并用 AOR（责任领域）清单和 GACCS 简报这类轻量框架来对齐营销和产品。最后，她分享职能专家如何把自己清晰、具体的价值贡献（比如帮创始人搭建营销职能）讲清楚，从而变成人人争抢的天使投资人。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Forget the product marketing content partner, demand and growth, forget all of it, and just think of marketing as you need a fuel and you need an engine. And goal is like all the things that you're creating. I mean this should be obvious, but it's the content, it's the word, it's the design in some regard. All the things that you're making, all the things that are going to add value. An engine is how you get it out to the right people. And all of the tracking of that and sort of the ops work I put under engine, everyone needs an engine.
turns.zh: 忘掉产品营销、内容合作、需求生成和增长这些说法吧，把这些都抛到一边，就把营销想成：你需要燃料，也需要引擎。燃料就是你正在创作的所有东西。这话听起来应该显而易见，但它就是那些内容、那些文案，某种程度上还有设计。你做出来的所有东西，所有能创造价值的东西。引擎则是你如何把这些东西送到对的人面前的方式。而所有这些追踪工作，以及那些运营类的活儿，我都归到引擎这一类——反正每个人都需要一个引擎。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And the question is, where do you have the biggest challenge right now? Or where do you think if you did more, you would grow faster? Is it on fuel side or is on the engine side?
turns.zh: 而问题是：你眼下最大的挑战在哪儿？或者说，你觉得如果在某个方面多下点功夫，你就能增长得更快？是在燃料这一侧，还是在引擎这一侧？

turns.speaker: Lenny

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: She also writes my favorite newsletter on marketing, MKT1. And the best compliment that I can give her is that she's a marketer that thinks like a product manager. In our chat, Emily shares a ton of concrete advice on what to look for in your first marketing hire, what the different archetypes of marketers are, and who you should look for based on your business model. How to work with marketing effectively as a product team, and also what red flags to look for that tell you that your marketing team is not doing a great job.

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Emily is super specific and incredibly concrete with her advice, including sharing a ton of templates that you can immediately use that we link to in the share rooms. I always learn a ton talking to Emily and I can't wait for you to hear this episode. And so with that, I bring you Emily Kramer. I'm excited to chat with my friend John Cutler, from Podcast Sponsor Amplitude. Hey John.

turns.en: Hey Lenny. Excited to be here.

turns.speaker: Lenny

turns.zh: John，给我们讲讲 Amplitude 背后的故事吧。大多数人一想到 Amplitude 就会想到产品分析，但现在你们也开始做实验，甚至刚推出了一个 CDP。你们是怎么想的？

Experiment in CDP came out of listening to and observing our customers.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们一直把 Amplitude 定位成支持完整的产品闭环。想想看：收集数据、据此获得洞察、发布实验、从中学习。这就是我们心中增长的核心。所以我们最大的那个"啊哈"时刻，是看到有那么多客户在用 Amplitude 分析实验、用分群去做触达、把数据发往其他目的地。实验和 CDP 就是来自倾听和观察我们的客户。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And supporting growth and learning has always been amplitude's core focus, right?
turns.zh: 而支持增长和学习一直是 Amplitude 的核心重点，对吧？

turns.speaker: John Cutler
turns.en: Yeah. So Amplitude tries to meet customers where they are. We just launched starter templates and have a great scholarship program for startups. There's never been a more important time for growth.
turns.zh: 对。所以 Amplitude 总是尽量在客户所在的地方接住他们。我们刚推出了入门模板，还有一个很棒的面向初创公司的奖学金计划。现在对增长来说，从来没比今天更重要的时刻了。

I'm really excited to be chatting with you.
turns.zh: 如果你在观望一个新机会，无论主动还是被动，都来加入这个社群吧。它是免费的，你可以匿名，甚至可以把自己在特定公司面前隐藏起来。你也可以随时退出，而且你只会收到你想听的那些公司的消息。去看看 lennysjobs.com/talent。Emily，欢迎来到这档播客，我真的很高兴能跟你聊聊。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Yeah. Thanks for having me. Looking forward to chatting with you in depth here.
turns.zh: 是啊，谢谢你邀请我。很期待在这儿跟你深入地聊一聊。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So if I remember correctly, we first met in the first round Angel Track program maybe two years ago, and then since then we've invested in a bunch of different companies together. I'm also just a big fan of your newsletter that we're going to chat about. So just to settle little context for folks, can you just give us a quick high level overview of your illustrious career and then also just plug your newsletter so folks can find it.
turns.zh: 如果我没记错的话，我们应该是第一轮 Angel Track 项目时认识的，大概两年前？从那以后我们一起投了好几家不同的公司。而且我本身就超喜欢你那份我们要聊的通讯。那么先给听众一点背景吧，你能快速、高屋建瓴地讲讲你辉煌的职业生涯，顺便也宣传一下你的通讯，方便大家找到它？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: For sure. And theme of my career has been building out marketing teams at B2B startups. So early in my career I was in advertising, went to business school. But after that I started doing the startup thing and I was at Ticketfly, I was like the second marketer. And then I went to Asana where I was the first marketer when they were about 30, 35 people and built up that team and led the team for just under four years. And then I went to a small seed funded company, help them raise rates and eventually went to Carta, which was about 300 people when I joined-ish give or take, but didn't have a marketing function at the time.
turns.zh: 没问题。我职业生涯的主线，就是在 B2B 初创公司搭建营销团队。早年间我在广告行业，后来去了商学院。但那之后我就开始了创业这件事，先去了 Ticketfly，我是那时候第二个市场人员。然后我去了 Asana，在他们大概三四十人的时候我是第一个市场人员，把那支团队搭建起来并带了近四年。之后我去了一家拿种子轮的小公司，帮他们把估值做起来，后来去了 Carta——我加入时大概 300 人左右，上下浮动不大，但那时候公司还没有营销职能。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: So built that function up from scratch. Much like Asana but at a very different stage in the company's life cycle. And then since then I've been advising and investing full time and now have a small fund where we invest in early stage B2B and help them build out marketing. So building marketing, that's what I do.
turns.zh: 所以我是从零开始把那个职能搭起来的。跟 Asana 很像，只是公司处在完全不同的生命周期阶段。从那以后，我就全职做顾问和投资，现在还有一个小基金，我们投早期 B2B 公司，帮他们搭建营销。所以，搭建营销，这就是我做的事。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love it. Okay, so plug your fund and your newsletter real quick just so we can cover that.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这个。好，那赶紧宣传一下你的基金和通讯，这样我们就覆盖到了。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Oh yeah, sorry about that. My newsletter is the letters mkt1.substack.com and my fund is Market 1 Capital. You can pretty much find most of these things on mkt1.co. Links to all the different various things that I'm doing so I can remember, because there's lots of iron in the fire. So got to keep the website up to date so I don't lose track of all the things that are going on. I also have a job board and a bunch of other things. You have more things going on but I have a number of set of things.
turns.zh: 哦对，差点忘了。我的通讯是 mkt1.substack.com，我的基金叫 Market 1 Capital。基本上在 mkt1.co 上都能找到我做的这些事。我把各种在做的事情都链上去了，不然我自己都记不住，因为手头摊子太多了。得把网站更新好，免得把自己在做的所有事弄丢了。我还有一个招聘板和一堆别的东西。你摊子更多，但我这儿也攒了一堆事。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. And we'll link to that in the show notes and everything. I don't think I've told you this but many founders have mentioned you as one of their most helpful angel investors that they've had on their cap table. It just comes up often when we co-invest. And the things that you help them most with as far as I understand is marketing advice, go to market advice, hiring marketing people. And so, I'd love to spend most of our time chatting through, basically the advice that you give founders around marketing.
turns.zh: 太棒了。我们会在节目备注里都链上。我好像从没跟你说过，但很多创始人提到你时，都说你是他们股东席上最有帮助的那种天使投资人。我们共同投资的时候，这事儿经常冒出来。据我所知，你帮他们最多的地方就是营销建议、走向市场建议、招营销的人。所以，我很想把我们大部分时间花在聊你给创始人的那些营销建议上。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And the first area I wanted to dig into is hiring marketing people. To non-marketing people it's such a mystery of just like, what is a marketing person? What do I expect from them? How do I hire them? How do I find them? How do I interview them? What should I avoid? So my first question is just like what mistakes have you seen founders and teams make when they're thinking about marketing and hiring marketing people?
turns.zh: 我想先深挖的第一个领域就是招营销的人。对不懂营销的人来说，这简直像个谜：什么是市场人员？我对他们有什么期待？怎么招？怎么找？怎么面试？什么该避坑？所以我的第一个问题就是：你见过创始人和团队在思考营销、招聘营销人员时，都犯过哪些错误？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And just to add to that, it's even hard for marketers to hire other marketers. It's even confusing for marketers to know where they fit in. And if they haven't been hired yet exactly what world they should be looking at or exactly who else they should be hired on the team. While it's very confusing for founders and people who haven't kind of been in a larger marketing team to understand all the different function, like also confusing for marketers. And I think that's just because there's so many different sub functions of marketing and there's so many different things that marketers could do.
turns.zh: 而且得补充一句，连市场人员自己招市场人员都很难。市场人员自己要搞清楚自己该往哪儿摆，都很混乱。要是还没被招进去，具体该看哪个方向、团队里还该招谁，他们也未必清楚。对创始人和那些没在大型营销团队待过的人来说，搞懂那些五花八门的功能已经够乱了，其实对市场人员自己也一样乱。我觉得原因就是营销有太多不同的子职能，市场人员能做的事也太多了。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And there's such a range of being a deep specialist. You have people that are just deep SEO specialists or deep paid search specialists or writers and they love to write and they write long form content and that's definitely a part of what marketing does, but it's a specialty for sure. And then you have people that are just very much generalists and can handle all areas of marketing. So a couple of mistakes that I see is just hiring people that don't cover the area that you need most as a startup. And that kind of comes for two reasons.
turns.zh: 而且这个光谱跨度极大，从深度专家到什么都懂的都有。有些人就是深度的 SEO 专家，或者深度的付费搜索专家，或者写手——他们爱写，写长文内容，那确实是营销的一部分，但绝对是个专门领域。然后还有些人是非常通才型的，能 handle 住营销的所有板块。所以我常看到的一个错误，就是招了根本覆盖不到你作为初创公司最需要那块的人。这又源于两个原因。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: One, is like you don't know as a founder or someone else doing a marketing hiring for the first person, you don't know what you're going to be doing in marketing. You don't know what your big levers are going to be, you don't know what's going to work. And so you hire a marketer thinking they're like smart, they've done this before. But really they haven't done the thing that you need to do before. So I see that especially with business model where I think having the right business model experience is almost more important than having industry experience or experience with that audience.
turns.zh: 一是，作为创始人或者第一次做营销招聘的人，你根本不知道自己在营销上要做什么。你不知道你的大杠杆在哪、不知道什么会奏效。于是你招了个市场人员，觉得这人挺聪明、以前干过。但其实他们以前根本没干过你需要的那件事。所以我特别在商业模式上看到这点：我觉得有对的商业模式经验，比有行业经验或者对那类受众的经验重要得多。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And I think often people are like, I need someone who is marketed to HR or marketed to construction or that specific. And my response is you, you're going to really narrow your set up people with that, and also it doesn't matter as much because great marketers learn the audience and learn the product quickly. And sometimes that fresh set of eyes is helpful and you have other experts in house on the audience. But the business model really dictates what marketing does in a big way. And by business model I mean more like, are you doing top down sales? Are you selling the enterprise?
turns.zh: 而且我发现大家经常说"我需要个给 HR 做过营销的、或者给建筑业做过营销的、或者某个特定人群做过的人"。我的回应是：你这么搞，会把候选人池缩得特别窄，而且这事儿没那么重要，因为优秀的市场人员能很快搞懂受众、搞懂产品。有时候这种新鲜的视角反而有帮助，而且你内部本来就有懂受众的专家。但商业模式是真的在很大程度上决定了营销该做什么。我说的商业模式，更像是指：你们做的是自上而下的销售吗？你们卖企业客户吗？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Are you doing bottom up product led growth or have a free version? Or whatever it is. Those types of things matter a lot. Because the set of marketing activities is just wildly different which I'm sure we'll go into. So to kind of summarize here, what I'd tell founders is I usually start when I talk to founders about who you need to hire in marketing. Because usually the question is, I think I need a marketer, who do I hire? And my critic question, let's try to nail this down because there isn't one answer. It very much depends.
turns.zh: 你们做的是自下而上的产品驱动增长，还是有免费版？还是别的什么形态？这些类型的事差别巨大。因为营销活动的那一套完全不一样——这点我们后面肯定会展开。所以总结一下，我对创始人想说的是：创始人来问我"我需要招个市场人员，该招谁"的时候，我通常会从"你到底需要招营销里的哪类人"开始聊。因为通常问题就是"我觉得我需要个市场人员，招谁？"而我的反问是：咱们先把这事儿定下来，因为这没有标准答案，非常取决于具体情况。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: There's usually some common archetypes. But the first thing I say is forget all the sub-functions that you've heard about in marketing. Forget the product marketing content marketing partner, demand and growth, forget all of it and just think of marketing as you need fuel and you need an engine. And the goal is all the things that you're creating. I mean this should be obvious, but it's the content, it's the word that's the design and some regard, it's all the things you're making, all the things that are going to add value.
turns.zh: 通常会有一些常见的画像。但我说的第一件事就是：忘掉你听过的那些营销子职能吧。忘掉产品营销、内容营销、合作、需求生成和增长，把这些全抛掉，就把营销想成：你需要燃料，也需要引擎。目标就是你在创造的所有东西。这话应该显而易见，但就是那些内容、那些文案、那些设计，某种程度上，就是你正在做的所有东西，所有能创造价值的东西。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: An engine is how you get it out to the right people. And all of the tracking of that And of the ops work I put under engine. So you still need an engine. And the question is, where do you have the biggest challenge right now or where do you think if you did more, you would grow faster? Is it on fuel side or is on the engine side? Typically, if you just think about it logically, you kind of need the fuel first. And sometimes what I see is people just build an engine first and they're like why isn't this working we're sending so many outbound emails? And it's like, well you don't have anything valuable to put in those, you have no fuel so this isn't working.
turns.zh: 引擎是你怎么把东西送到对的人面前的方式。所有的追踪工作，还有运营类的工作，我都归到引擎下。所以你还是需要引擎。问题是：你眼下最大的挑战在哪儿，或者说你觉得在哪个方面多投入，增长会更快？是在燃料这一侧，还是引擎这一侧？通常，只要逻辑上想一下，你大概得先有燃料。但我有时会看到人们先搭了个引擎，然后纳闷"这怎么不奏效？我们都发了那么多外呼邮件了"。我就说：你里面根本没有什么有价值的东西可放，你没有燃料，所以这当然不奏效。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Or you see the flip side where they're making a whole bunch of things, they're writing a bunch of blog quotes or making a bunch of content and they're like, this content doesn't work. It's like, we'll, have you tried distributing it? Because if you're not distributing that and getting mileage out of it's a waste of time. So this is a big problem in marketing overall, getting the balance of fuel and engine rate. But I like to start from what do you think is going to help most and what skillset does your team not have? And typically, if a team is sales driven top down, they might have an SDR or at least two at this time.
turns.zh: 或者你看到反面：他们做了一大堆东西，写了好多博客语录、生产了一堆内容，然后说"这内容不奏效"。我就说：嗯，你试过分发它吗？因为如果你不分发出去、从中榨出价值，那就是在浪费时间。所以整体来说，营销里一个大问题就是燃料和引擎的比例失衡。但我喜欢从一个问题切入：你觉得什么最能帮到你？你的团队缺的是什么技能？通常，如果一个团队是销售驱动、自上而下的，他们这个时候可能已经有个 SDR，或者至少两个。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Usually that comes first in top down. And so the SDRs are kind of an engine. They're an imperfect engine, outbound shouldn't be the only thing you're doing. And if they're just reaching out and asking people to schedule meetings, it might not be that effective but you have a little engine going on. So maybe now you need some fuel first. On the other side of it, if you're a product growth or bottom up, you might have a situation where just nothing is optimized. Your website's conversion rates are terrible, people are dropping out of the funnel all over the place.
turns.zh: 通常自上而下模式里，这步先走。所以 SDR 也算一种引擎。不过是不太完美的引擎，外呼不该是你唯一在做的事。如果他们只是去触达、约人开会，可能没那么有效，但至少你有个小引擎在转。所以也许这时候你先需要点燃料。反过来看，如果你做的是产品增长、自下而上，你可能会遇到一种情况：什么都没被优化。你网站的转化率烂透了，用户在漏斗各个地方流失。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And you really need someone who can build up these lifecycle email touches, work in product instead of work with a product or a person as well. And you really just need more engine because people are already finding out about your product or it has someone made virality and you're just not capturing enough of that. So I kind of like decode, what's going to help the most right now? And then ideally you get someone, so move back to an engine first.
turns.zh: 你真的需要有人能搭建起这些生命周期邮件触达，深耕产品内部而不只是跟产品团队配合。你真的就需要更多引擎，因为人们已经在发现你的产品了，或者它已经带上了某种病毒传播性，而你只是没把它接住、利用好。所以我喜欢先解码：眼下什么最能帮到你？然后理想情况下你招到一个人——那就先回到引擎这边。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Can I actually jump in real quick because that's a really cool framework that I haven't heard before, this idea of fuel and engine from a marketing perspective. To make it a little more concrete, what are a examples of, it doesn't have to be exhaustive, but when you think about all the things that could be fueled, and all the types of engines, what are those lists?
turns.zh: 我能插一句吗，因为刚才那个框架真的太酷了，我以前没听过——就是这种从营销角度区分"燃料"和"引擎"的思路。为了更具体一点，能举些例子吗？不用穷尽，但当你想所有可以当作燃料的东西，以及所有类型的引擎，这两个清单分别是什么？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: For sure. Yeah, I have a diagram of this stuff in my newsletter.
turns.zh: 当然。对，我在通讯里画过一张这方面的图。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. We'll link to that.
turns.zh: 太棒了，我们会把链接放上去。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: So when I think about fuel and engine and what goes on either side, it's important to recognize that some things are fuel or engine and that some things are both fuel and engine. Let me start with an example of something that's fuel and engine. If done well, your community, let's just take for instance, let's keep it simple because community needs 75 things. If you have a Slack community that should be tool and engine. If you have people creating content in there that maybe you can then use in other areas. Like you do this well, you take what's going on in your community and you do your community wisdom parts of your newsletter.
turns.zh: 所以当我思考燃料和引擎、以及两边各放什么的时候，关键是要认识到：有些东西是燃料，有些是引擎，还有些既是燃料又是引擎。我先从既是燃料又是引擎的例子说起。如果做得好，你的社区就是——就拿这个举例吧，咱们简单点，因为社区要操心的事有一大堆。如果你有个 Slack 社区，它应该既是工具也是引擎。如果里面有用户在产内容，你之后还能用在其他地方。比如你做得好，就把社区里发生的事拿过来，做成你通讯里的"社区智慧"板块。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: So you're using that as fuel but it's also an engine because you have people in your audience that you can distribute out content too. So there's some examples like that. But to go back to the question of what fuel and what's an engine. Fuel is like the copy on your website, it's the blog posts that you had, it's the templates that you've created. It's the video recordings of the webinars or the podcast. It's basically content, but also to include some of the copy.
turns.zh: 所以你把它当燃料在用，但它也是引擎，因为你受众里有人，你可以把内容分发给他们。就是这类例子。不过回到"什么是燃料、什么是引擎"这个问题。燃料就像是你网站上的文案，是你写的博客文章，是你做出来的模板。是网络研讨会或者播客的视频录像。基本上就是内容，但也包括一部分文案。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And I think people have this limited view of contents where they think blog posts and blog posts are still one part of content. Content should be tools, resource, assembled like calculators, those kind of things do better in all the cases.
turns.zh: 我觉得人们对内容有种狭隘的看法，以为内容就是博客文章——博客文章当然仍是内容的一部分。但内容应该包括工具、资源，像计算器这种组合型的东西，这些在任何情况下都表现更好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And positioning I imagine is a fuel.
turns.zh: 那定位（positioning）我想应该算燃料吧。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Yeah. That's some of the product marketing steps. So product marketing is this weird thing and we'll talk about it that's kind of in the middle. But yes, product marketing, doing any positioning. Again, like the web copy which is of the first manifestation of your positioning and messaging, or it should be the source of truth for all of that. But you're positioning, you are messaging the words, the words are the things you're creating, that's the fuel, things that add value in that way. The engine side is what people tend to call marketing growth or demand jam or things of that nature.
turns.zh: 对，那是产品营销里的一些步骤。产品营销是个有点怪的东西，我们待会儿会聊，它处在中间地带。但没错，产品营销、做任何定位——再比如网站文案，它是你定位和信息的第一个呈现，或者说它应该是所有这些东西的"真相之源"。而你的定位、你的信息传达、那些措辞，那些你创造出来的字句，就是燃料，是那种能创造价值的东西。引擎这一侧，就是人们通常叫营销增长、或者需求生成（demand gen）、或者类似性质的东西。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: That's really the distribution channels. The email copy itself is fuel, but how you've set up the email and the segmentation you've used and the rules for that drip email, that's the engine. The SEO content is fuel, but your SEO sort of keyword list as a technical FTO and that kind of stuff is sort of engine. Social media, you got to have good fuel but you also have to nail it exactly what channels you're using and all that stuff. So a lot of things have both sides of it. So most projects or activities or initiative have some fuel and some engine.
turns.zh: 那其实就是分发渠道。邮件文案本身是燃料，但你是怎么搭建这封邮件的、你用的分群、还有这封自动序列邮件（drip email）的规则，那才是引擎。SEO 内容是燃料，但你的 SEO 关键词清单、技术性的优化之类的东西，算是引擎。社交媒体，你得有好的燃料，但也得精准搞定你到底用哪些渠道等等。所以很多东西两面都有。大多数项目、活动或者计划，都有一面燃料、一面引擎。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: I also consider marketing ops work, the setup of HubSpot or whatever it is you might be using. That's engine. It's really instructing the engine, but I kind of put it in that bucket. Because people who are usually good at executing on email or executing on ads or things like that, usually have some working knowledge of the ops work and the reporting work because you have to be optimizing. I guess admin paid is also engine.
turns.zh: 我也把营销运营的工作算作引擎，比如搭建 HubSpot 或者你用的任何工具。那是引擎——其实是"给引擎下指令"，但我把它归到那个桶里。因为通常擅长执行邮件、执行广告这类事的人，一般都对运营和报告工作有点实操知识，毕竟你总得优化。我想付费广告管理也算引擎。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. Okay. And so coming back to your original piece of advice here is before hiring a marketing person, you want to figure out which of these buckets is the biggest constraint to your growth, right?
turns.zh: 太棒了。好，回到你最初的建议：在招市场人员之前，你想先搞清楚这几个桶里哪一个是对你增长最大的制约，对吧？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You talked about this briefly, but is there any simple heuristics to give you a sense of it's probably fuel, I need more great content, maybe some website updates versus I need to figure out how to get this out. How do you think about that high level?
turns.zh: 你简单提过这个，但有没有什么简单的启发式判断，能让人感觉出来"这大概是燃料问题，我需要更多好内容、可能再改改网站"，还是"我得搞明白怎么把它推出去"？你从高层是怎么想的？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Yeah, I mean, it's kind of simple. You can just ask what are your top performing pieces of content or what's the top performing page on your website or things of that feature. Who is your product for? Why is it better? What are the benefits? How does it compare to competitors? If you don't have an answer for those questions, you don't have top performing content and you don't know your positioning and all that stuff, you got a fuel problem here. Oh, you wrote this really great piece of content and I saw it on your website, how are you distributing that? What are you doing?
turns.zh: 对，其实挺简单的。你就问：你表现最好的内容是什么？或者你网站上表现最好的页面是哪个？你们的产品是给谁用的？为什么更好？有什么好处？跟竞品比怎么样？如果你回答不上这些问题，说明你既没有表现好的内容、也不知道自己的定位等等，那你这儿就是燃料问题。哦，你写了篇特别好的内容，我在你网站上看到了，那你是怎么分发的？你在做什么？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And they're like, I shared it on social, they didn't really go anywhere, you got an engine problem. Or if I say, do you know what your final stages are? You have two sales people now, how does the marketing sales handoff go? They're like, they share a list and block off everyone they should reach out to. I'm like, well, you have an adventure problem if this isn't going to scale. So it's just these basic things. Are you doing these things or not? And sometimes founders are really great at making the original sort of content and writing the early positioning.
turns.zh: 然后他们说，我在社媒上发过，但没怎么传开，那你就是引擎问题。或者我说：你知道你的最终转化环节是什么吗？你现在有两个销售了，营销和销售的衔接是怎么做的？他们说，就共享一个名单，把该触达的人圈出来。我就说：如果这套没法规模化，那你就是衔接上会出问题。所以就是这些基本的事。你到底在做还是没在做？有时候创始人特别擅长做最原始那种内容、写早期的定位。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And they're the best suited to that and they just need someone to help them get that stuff out and that's when they need an engine person. So that's basically how you figure it out. And normally when you ask vendors that question, they get it pretty quickly. They're like, "Okay, I think this is my problem, I can kind of identify it." And then it's like, okay, from here, well, what exactly do you need and what exact type of marketer do you need? And that's where everyone's answer is always, I think I heard from investors or I've been hearing from other founders that I really need a product marketer.
turns.zh: 而他们最擅长这个，他们只是需要有人帮他们把那些东西推出去，这时候他们就需要一个做引擎的人。所以基本上你就是这么判断的。通常你一问创始人这个问题，他们很快就能 get 到。他们说："好吧，我觉得这就是我的问题，我能大致锁定它。"然后就进入下一步：好，那具体你需要什么、你需要哪种市场人员？而这时候所有人给出的答案永远都是：我觉得我从投资人那儿听说、或者从其他创始人那儿听说，我真的很需要一个产品营销（product marketer）。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And the question is, well what do you think a product marketer is? And you get a different answer every time. In fact, when I was at Asana our COO, his question that he liked to ask all the marketers or all the product marketers that we were interviewing was just, "What's product marketing?" And that's the scariest question you can ask a product marketer. It's like no scarier question for a product marketer then hey, what's a product marketer? They're like, "Oh, shit, I have no idea. Just my job, it's me. I'm a product marketer."
turns.zh: 而问题是：那你觉得产品营销到底是什么？每次得到的答案都不一样。其实我在 Asana 的时候，我们的 COO 特别爱问所有市场人员、或者所有来面试的产品营销一个问题是："产品营销是什么？"而对产品营销来说，这是最吓人的问题。对产品营销来说，没有比"嘿，产品营销是什么？"更吓人的问题了。他们会说："哦，靠，我完全不知道。这就是我的活儿啊，我就是产品营销。"

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: But really a product marketer, they understand the product, they understand the audience and they understand the market in which you're operating. And from there they can figure out how to communicate with your audience about the right things at the right time. So they're kind of laying groundwork. And then they're also doing some work too. They're also doing a lot of the copywriting and the actual messaging and handling sort of launches and sometimes writing copy for things like emails and helping set the content strategy and things like that.
turns.zh: 但真正的产品营销，是懂产品、懂受众、也懂你所在的市场。在此基础上，他们能想清楚怎么在对的时间、就对的主题跟你的受众沟通。所以他们是在打地基。同时他们也在做具体的工作。他们要做大量的文案写作、实际的信息传达、操盘发布，有时还要给邮件之类写文案，帮着定内容策略等等。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And people think they need product marketers. One because it's like a fake people say, but two, because product marketers tend to shadow this line between fuel and engine. They're more on the fuel side, but particularly they've done a lot of launches in the past. They have a general understanding of channel strategy and what channels do at what time and that sort of end and stuff. But product marketers aren't really specialists in writing and producing content. They're not specialists in building out marketing ops or doing FDO.
turns.zh: 人们觉得自己需要产品营销，一来是因为这词大家都在说、像是个流行标签，二来是因为产品营销往往游走在燃料和引擎这条分界线的两侧。他们更偏燃料这一侧，但尤其是他们过去做过很多发布。他们对渠道策略、以及不同渠道在不同时段起什么作用，有个整体性的理解。但产品营销并不是写内容、生产内容的专家，也不是搭建营销运营、或者做需求生成的专家。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: They're definitely more of the generalist function. And so sometimes that's a great answer. You need a product marketer, but sometimes you need someone that's scrappier in different areas. Another one of my frameworks is we start with doing these seal engine, what are the biggest problems? What are the biggest things that if you did, you would drive growth? And then we talk about the three typical subfunction that you would hire, which would be content, community type person, a growth demands and type person and a product marketer. And we kind of talk about what those three things mean.
turns.zh: 他们绝对更偏通才型职能。所以有时候"你需要一个产品营销"是个很好的答案。但有时候你需要的是在某个领域更能"土法上马"、更灵活的人。我的另一个框架是：我们先做这个燃料/引擎分析，最大的问题是什么？哪些事只要你做了就能带动增长？然后我们再聊你会招的三类典型子职能——内容型的人、社区型的人、增长需求型的人，以及一个产品营销。我们再细聊这三类分别意味着什么。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And kind of align based on what you're saying, based on the fuel engine thing, probably in this type of person. And then from there, what I tell people when you're hiring your first marketer and probably even your first several marketers, you're more want to hire generalist than specialists. This is probably true for anywhere at the early stage startup, but specialists are great to hire. It's great to hire contractors that are specialists. Like the FDO contractor, even the contractor who can write the marketing ops contractor. But you want someone who is pretty much a generalist.
turns.zh: 而且基本上，根据你说的、基于燃料引擎那套，你应该对齐到这一类人。然后从这儿出发，我跟大家说：在招你的第一个市场人员、甚至前几个市场人员时，你更想招的是通才而不是专才。在早期初创公司哪儿都说得通——但专才也很值得招，招专才型的合同工就很棒，比如做需求生成的合同工，甚至能做营销运营的合同工。但你想要的是一个基本是通才的人。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And the way I describe that within marketing, usually you you are like hire a T shape person that bites in one area and has working knowledge and try to crop all of them. But I use this thing that I made up which is you one up higher pie shaped marketers, not pie like dessert, but pie like 3.14 where the pie symbol has two vertical lines. So like a T but it has an extra line. And it's because you want the first marketer to be an expert in one of those three areas that I mentioned, product marketing, content marketing, growth marketing.
turns.zh: 我在营销里描述这个的方式通常是：招一个 T 型的人，在一个领域扎得很深，同时对其余领域有实操层面的了解。但我用的是我自己编的一个说法，叫"π 型（pie shaped）市场人员"——不是甜点那个 pie，而是 3.14 那个 π，π 这个符号有两条竖线。所以像个 T，但多了一条线。这是因为你希望第一个市场人员在我刚才说的三个领域里——产品营销、内容营销、增长营销——有一个是专家。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And you want them to be proficient in another one, the second T. But you want them to be able to set strategy and know how to hire contractors across all of them. And so the promise land of hiring a first marketer, they are a pie shape marketer. And so then you could hire a content and product marketing pie shape marketer, product marketing growth pie shape marketer. But it's like what are those two spikes and what's the one that you're going to worry less about that they need to work knowledge of?
turns.zh: 而且你希望他们在另一个领域也够熟练，就是第二条竖线。但你希望他们能定战略，并且知道怎么在所有这些领域里招合同工。所以招第一个市场人员的理想国，就是招到一个 π 型市场人员。接下来你可以招一个"内容+产品营销"的 π 型，或者"产品营销+增长"的 π 型。关键就是：那两根尖刺分别是什么？而第三块是你不太需要他们有实操知识、可以少操心的？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: The last thing I'll say on the pie piece is that it's really hard to find someone that's a content marketer that's also really good at growth. Like that pie shape marketer exists a lot less frequently. Maybe it's someone who is really amazing at content distribution or really amazing at FDO, but they don't really exist. Because the content side is like one side of the brain and the growth data stuff is a whole other side of the brain. You don't find those people very often. So you are usually looking for that product marketing, growth marketing pie shaped person or the product marketing content marketing pie shaped person.
turns.zh: 关于 π 型，我最后再说一点：很难找到一个既是内容营销、又在增长上真的很厉害的人。这种 π 型市场人员存在的概率要低得多。也许有人特别擅长内容分发、或者特别擅长需求生成，但这种人基本不存在。因为内容那一侧是大脑的一边，增长和数据那一侧完全是另一边。你不太常遇到这种人。所以你通常找的是"产品营销+增长营销"的 π 型，或者"产品营销+内容营销"的 π 型。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, okay. This is great. So I was going to ask you about-
turns.zh: 哇，好，这太棒了。我本来想问你关于——

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Sorry this is dense, this is a lot of marketing window, so hopefully we're breaking it down.
turns.zh: 抱歉，这块信息密度很大，一下子塞了很多营销框架，希望我们把它拆开了讲。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, we're getting there. So let me try to summarize and see where we go. So I was going to ask you about the archetypes of marketing people and it sounds like there's these three is the way you think about it. There's basically a content community person, there's a growth person and then there's product marketing which is kind of like in the middle. And I guess, one question I wanted to ask is there's also just the growth function, product growth, growth PMs, things like that. Do you see that as the same thing as this growth marketing person or is that a different type of person and a different role?
turns.zh: 对，我们慢慢来。让我试着总结一下，看看接下来往哪走。我本来想问你关于市场人员的画像，听起来你心里是这三类：基本上有内容/社区型的人、有增长型的人，然后还有处在中间的产品营销。我想问的一个问题是：还有那种增长职能，比如产品增长、增长 PM 之类的。你觉得那跟这个增长营销的人是一回事吗，还是说那是一种不同类型的人、不同的角色？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: In top down sales businesses it is 100% different. A growth person typically probably called a demand gen person. There's a whole other rabbit hole we can go down on what's the difference between growth marketing and demand gen. And demand gen is probably more top of funnel and growth marketing is probably more full funnel at its simplest form. But it's definitely different there. In a product led growth business, the growth marketer and the product grows sort of role or the hybrid growth role, sometimes it can be the same person depending on the skill.
turns.zh: 在自上而下的销售型业务里，那是 100% 不同的。增长型的人通常可能被叫做需求生成（demand gen）的人。关于增长营销和需求生成的区别，我们可以深究到另一个兔子洞里去。最简单的说法，需求生成更偏漏斗顶部，增长营销更偏全漏斗。但那块绝对是不同的。在产品驱动增长（PLG）的业务里，增长营销和那个"产品增长"角色、或者混合增长角色，有时候可以是同一个人，取决于技能。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: But typically the difference would be that the growth marketer is doing more of the top of funnel sort of inbound side and the product growth person is doing more once they actually get into the product, but can be collaborated with that growth marketer. So it can be the same person in extremely data driven sort of person that kind of has the working knowledge of both marketing and product stuff. It can be one person in early stage PLG companies.
turns.zh: 但通常区别在于：增长营销做的是更多漏斗顶部、入站那一侧，而产品增长做的是用户真正进到产品之后那一段——不过这俩可以跟增长营销协作。所以在一个极度数据驱动、对营销和产品两边都有实操知识的人身上，它可以是同一个人。在早期 PLG 公司里，它可以是一个人。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: But I think typically, and I'm sure you've seen that at larger companies as you get bigger, you're going to have some people that come from more of that marketing perspective and you're going to have a little bit come from more of that product perspective. But the question is, is there ever one person that does that?
turns.zh: 但我觉得通常——你也肯定在大公司里见过，随着公司变大，你会有些更偏营销视角的人，也会有些更偏产品视角的人。但问题是：真有能一个人把两边全干了的吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, so to make this a little more concrete even for startups, thinking from a startup perspective, when you're just thinking about hiring your first say marketing person. When you think about this set of buckets that you talked about, there's content marketing, growth marketing, product marketing, plus to your point there's at larger companies or maybe later stages separate from a growth PM type person. What do you generally think is the right role to hire/architect to focus on? Or is it really dependent like you said on fuel versus engine versus something else?
turns.zh: 好，那为了让初创公司也能更具体点，从初创的视角想：当你在想招第一个市场人员时。考虑到你刚才说的那几个桶——内容营销、增长营销、产品营销，再加上你说的，在大公司或者更后期会跟增长 PM 这种角色分开。一般来说你觉得该招哪个角色、重点布局哪个？还是说真的就像你说的，取决于燃料还是引擎、还是别的什么？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: I mean it's highly dependent on, again the business model, what you need more of, what you already have in place, what's going on. But the most common archetype that I say you want to hire is a product marketer. Even though I joke that everyone says you need a product marketer. But it's actually understanding what that is first, that understands growth marketing as well. So they probably work somewhere early on where they've had to have some exposure to that. So they understand all the channels they're working with, understand what they can do with those channels and maybe they need to work with contractors on some of those things.
turns.zh: 这个，高度取决于——再说一遍——商业模式、你更缺哪块、你现在已经有什么、现状如何。但我最常推荐大家招的画像，是产品营销。虽然我开玩笑说每个人都说你需要产品营销。但关键是先真正理解那是什么，而且这个人也要懂增长营销。所以他们大概早年某个时候待过的地方，让他们不得不接触过那块。所以他们懂自己手上的所有渠道，懂能用这些渠道做什么，也许某些事上他们需要跟合同工配合。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Also product marketer needs to know how to write. All marketers should some working knowledge in writing, but they need to know how to write. They are the copywriter for a long time. Tests that they can write, make sure they can write well, short form and long form. They're not going to be necessarily as good in writing as say a content person, but they need to be able to write. And product marketers just tend to have that ability to write and that ability to understand what channels they can use to reach their audience so they're in the middle. So often that's the case.
turns.zh: 还有，产品营销必须懂怎么写。所有市场人员都该对写作有点实操知识，但他们得真的会写。他们长期就是那个写文案的人。要测他们能不能写，确保他们短文、长文都写得不错。他们写的可能不一定像内容型的人那么好，但他们必须能写。而产品营销往往就既有这种写作能力，又有理解"能用哪些渠道触达受众"的能力，所以他们处在中间。所以常常就是这种情况。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: But I mean, sometimes I find that I'm recommending hiring that growth person first because they maybe already have a couple of really great contractors and they have a couple of really great pieces of content that can just be gifts that keep on giving if they keep distributing them and repurposing them.
turns.zh: 但我的意思是，有时候我发现我会建议先招那个增长型的人，因为他们可能已经有了几个特别好的合同工，也已经攒了几篇特别好的内容——只要持续分发、重新利用，这些就是会一直下金蛋的礼物。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What do you look for in this product marketing person? You mentioned ability to write is really important? What else? When someone's scanning LinkedIn or just later talking to them, what do you find is important to focus on and look for?
turns.zh: 那你在这个产品营销身上看重什么？你刚提到写作能力很重要？还有别的吗？当有人在刷 LinkedIn，或者之后跟他们聊的时候，你觉得该重点聚焦、重点看的是什么？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: This can be hard to find, but I think I want to see that they've worked on a team that's early enough where they are not siloed into their specific role. Because what happens at leader stage companies or at public companies is when you're a product marketer, you don't see what's going on in the rest of marketing at all. You have a very siloed view of it, maybe you're only working on product launches as a product marketer, which the positioning is already set, the audience research already done, they haven't done any of those things, or the channels are all built out.
turns.zh: 这个挺难找的，但我想看到的是：他们待过的团队足够早期，以至于他们没有被困在自己那个具体角色里。因为在头部公司或者上市公司，当你是个产品营销时，你根本看不到营销其他部分在发生什么。你的视角非常孤岛化，也许你作为产品营销只做产品发布，而定位早就定好了、受众调研早就做完了，这些事他们一件没做过，或者渠道全都搭好了。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: It's just different. I think that's the case in a lot of roles at startups. But building it from scratch is different. So that doesn't mean that if you're a series A company hiring your first marketer that you need to hire someone that's worked at a Series A company. But it usually means you're hiring someone that's worked at least at a growth stage company where they have exposure to a bunch of various marketing. Also looking for, have they seen what great looks like? So whether they joined us startup up early and it did really well, or whether that's they had a stint at a later stage company and then earliest in their career, they're a big company then they went to some big smaller.
turns.zh: 那完全不一样。我觉得很多初创角色都是这样。但从零搭建是不同的。所以这并不意味着如果你是 A 轮公司、在招第一个市场人员，你就得招一个在 A 轮公司干过的人。但它通常意味着你招的是一个至少在成长期公司待过、对各种营销都有过接触的人。另外我也在看：他们见过"什么是好"吗？不管是他们早年加入了一家早期初创、而且它做得很成功，还是他们在更后期公司待过一阵、或者职业生涯最早是在大公司、后来又去了某家稍小的。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Do they know what high quality sort of great looks like? It doesn't always have to be, you don't have to have been at a startup that everyone thinks of as like, they're really great at marketing, but it is helpful. And there are some people that just have a really high quality bar and really understand what great marketing looks like even if they haven't worked in those companies. But I like to say has worked somewhere early enough that they could set strategy across all of marketing. And do they know what great looked like? That's something I'm scanning for. I'm also scanning for your first marketer, you don't want to go out, I see this mistake all the time.
turns.zh: 他们知道什么是高质量、什么是"好"吗？这不一定非得是——你不必非得待过一家大家都觉得"营销做得特别棒"的初创，但有那经历会有帮助。也有些人就是有很高的质量门槛，哪怕没在那些公司干过，也真的懂什么是好营销。但我喜欢说：得在足够早期的地方待过，以至于他们能给整个营销定战略。而且他们知道"好"长什么样吗？这是我在筛的。我还会筛的是：招你的第一个市场人员，你别出去——我老看到这个错误。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: You don't want to go out and hire someone super senior who's only worked at a public company. That's the wrong person. And often VCs or sort lead investors that aren't in a certain niche. when they refer candidates to startups, usually the fail I see is they're like, here's someone great from Google. And I'm like, I'm sure they're great but they're not great for this role and that's the mistake I see all the time. Oh, we just fired our first marketer. I'm like, "where did they work?" They're like, "They only worked at Salesforce." I'm like, well, yeah.
turns.zh: 你别出去招一个只在上市公司干过的、超资深的人。那是不对的人。而且经常是那些不在某个细分领域的 VC 或者牵头投资人，当他们给初创推荐候选人时，我通常看到的失败案例是：他们说"这儿有个从 Google 来的牛人"。我就说：我信他们牛，但他们不适合这个角色——这就是我经常看到的错误。"哦，我们刚把第一个市场人员开了。"我就问："他们之前在哪儿干的？"他们说："只在 Salesforce 干过。"我就说：嗯，那当然。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Why is that not a good fit?
turns.zh: 为什么那样不合适？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: Just because they don't understand how all the marketing works together and they don't understand how they built the foundation. It's much different marketing something that already everybody knows what it is or everybody knows the brand even if they don't know the product and they have a built in customer base, than building something up for scratch from scratch is just a very different marketing motion, and you need to do a lot of things. You need to do a lot of things yourself, you need to be a doer.
turns.zh: 就因为他们不懂所有营销是怎么协同运转的，也不懂地基是怎么打起来的。营销一个大家都已经知道它是什么、或者哪怕不知道产品但知道品牌、而且还有现成客户群的东西，跟从零开始把一样东西做起来，那完全是两种不同的营销打法。后者你得做非常多的事。很多事得你自己来，你得是个实干家。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: So you're really looking for most roles or most lead of function roles at startups, they need to be both strategic and of scrappy enough to get the work done. You're going to be doing it all. And in marketing you're often going to be the first marketer for a little while and you're going to be doing everything. And so there has to be some sign that you're going to be comfortable with that.
turns.zh: 所以你在初创招大多数角色、或者大多数职能负责人角色时，真正要找的是：既能定战略、又足够"土法上马"能把活干完的人。你会什么都得干。在营销里，你往往会在相当一段时间里是第一个市场人员，什么都得做。所以必须得有一些迹象表明你能从容应对这个。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. When do you find that it's usually best to hire your first marketing person?
turns.zh: 太棒了。你觉得通常什么时机招第一个市场人员最好？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: I mean stage wise you're looking at some nice people hire at seed depending on their business, but usually it's in Series A or you hire one sort of more junior person at seed when you're coming into raising or Series A and then you know have two people right after your Series A. But really, I think it's helpful to have some sort of semblance of product market fit. Maybe you're not 100% sure, but maybe you have definitely some successful customers. It's not like we're working with a design partner to build this out and we have a couple pilots. Marketing is really good at accelerating growth and doing that scale one to many.
turns.zh: 从阶段来说，有些人会根据自己的业务在种子轮就招，但通常是 A 轮，或者你在临近融资、要进 A 轮时在种子轮先招一个更初级的人，然后 A 轮一结束就有两个人了。但我真正觉得有帮助的是：得有某种程度的产品市场契合（PMF）的雏形。也许你不是 100% 确定，但至少你肯定有了一些成功的客户。不是说"我们正跟设计合作伙伴一起搭这个、有几个试点"。营销特别擅长加速增长、做那种一对多的规模化。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: So if you're still in the very well spoke founder led sales, founder led marketing, like I'm doing discovery with each of these potential customers and have to modify my product for them, that kind of thing. You don't need one yet. Founders can do a fair amount of stuff and they can use some contractors. I think you need them earlier in product growth models because you're not going to hire a salesperson then. So it's more thinking about go to market holistically and saying, do I need one or two people here and why is that? And so if you're a top down model sort of enterprise sale, you're probably going to have a couple sales people before you hire marketing, but that might not be the case.
turns.zh: 所以如果你还处在那种很典型的创始人主导销售、创始人主导营销的阶段——比如我正跟每个潜在客户做需求发现、还得为他们改我的产品，这种。那你暂时还不需要。创始人能搞定相当多的事，也能用些合同工。我觉得在 PLG 模型里你需要他们更早，因为你那时候不会去招销售。所以更多是整体性地思考走向市场，然后说：我这儿需要一两个人吗、为什么？所以如果你是自上而下的企业销售模型，你大概会在招营销之前先有几个销售，但也可能不是这样。

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: And these are more self or product led growth models, you just don't need the sales person. So having the marketer is helpful. So again, the business model affects this a lot, but usually the general rule of thumb is, if you had a marketer what would they do? And I often help people try to figure that out. What would they do and if they stepped on the gas and did all this stuff really well, would you be able to handle all those people that came in? Is it even a good time to bring all those people in to your product?
turns.zh: 而这些都是偏自助、或者产品驱动增长的模型，你根本不需要销售。所以有个市场人员就有帮助。所以再说一遍，商业模式对这影响很大，但通常的经验法则是：如果你有个市场人员，他们会做什么？我常帮人想清楚这点。他们会做什么——如果他们一脚油门、把这些事都做得特别好，你能接住那些涌进来的人吗？现在甚至是把那些人引到你产品里的好时机吗？

turns.speaker: Emily Kramer
turns.en: So are they going to be held back by where your product is or where some of the discovery on exact business model is or things like that. And that's the case. It's just not a good use money when they're kind of just sitting on their hands. I can't spend any money on paid and we don't even have any idea what to say on the website because we're selling four different things. It's just kind of hard to hire someone in that case.
turns.zh: 所以，他们是会被你产品的现状、或者某些关于具体商业模式的探索给拖住吗？如果是这样，那他们干坐着、只是浪费钱而已。我现在在付费上投不了任何钱，而且我们连网站上该说什么都没谱，因为我们在卖四种不同的东西。这种情况下招人就很尴尬。
